Up in the north, where the savannah lies,
Verse 1
A small little tuber, waiting to rise.
Frafra potato, some call it Salanga,
Hausa potato, in lands far away.
Small like a mint leaf, close to the ground,
A treasure of the north that's rarely found.
Once it fed the children, once it fed us all,
Verse 2
A delicacy sweeter than the rest, standing tall.
Now the young ones don't know its name,
Don't know how to grow it, what a shame.
An endangered crop, fading from the land,
It's time to bring it back, hand in hand.
Frafra potato, rise again,
Chorus
Feed our children, feed our men!
Small in size, but full of worth,
A gift once buried in the northern earth!
We are Acres, hear us say,
Bring Frafra potato back today!
Rich in carbohydrates, rich in fiber too,
Verse 3
Calcium and iron, B vitamins for you.
Even its leaves are a vegetable prize,
More protein there than the tuber supplies.
A short season crop, quick to yield,
A treasure hiding in a forgotten field.
Better than the sweet potato, some markets say,
Verse 4
More money in the harvest, more value each day.
Yet still we've let it slip away,
Time to plant it, time to say,
Grandmothers knew it, grandmothers grew it,
Now it's our turn to see it through.
Frafra potato, rise again,
